newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese parties demand release of union leader.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese parties demand release of union leader.

text.p: Lebanese political parties and labour unions demanded on Tuesday that the government release immediately a fiery leftist labour leader arrested five days ago.

Elias Abou Rizk, 54, is charged with impersonating the head of the General Labour Confederation (CGTL) and forcibly usurping office after disputed elections in April which split the labour movement and produced two rival CGTL leaderships.

The charges against Abou Rizk, who led a campaign of anti-government strikes and protests as CGTL leader from 1993-1997, were brought by his rival Ghneim al-Zoghbi whom the government recognised in April as the confederation's new head.
The charges carry jail terms of at least seven years.

The demand for his release came in a meeting of solidarity with Abou Rizk at which representatives of pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God), Islamic Jamaa (Group), Communist Party, right wing Phalangist Party, leftist opposition deputies and many other right and left wing parties were present.
"We demand the immediate release of Abou Rizk as this is his legitimate right," a statement by the gathering which was attended by 500 people said.

The former speaker of parliament deputy Husein al-Huseini, two former Prime Ministers deputies Selim al-Hoss and Omar Karami and Christian opposition deputies Nasib Lahoud and Butros Harb sent the meeting a message of solidarity.
